head: 19e3b23
target: Repos opt into the quiz gate with a committed .own-your-diff marker and a per-clone pre-push hook in .git/hooks, replacing the core.hooksPath=.githooks opt-in; quizgate sync stages quizgate on PATH and installs the hook in clones that carry the marker.
incidental: selftest moved from skills/own-your-diff/scripts/ to the repo-level scripts/ directory, and its SKILL.md line dropped
agent-mode.md wording: examiner subagents spawn fresh with none of your context
usage text of quizgate describing the new install and sync commands

questions.prompt: Why does the opt-in now live in a committed .own-your-diff marker with the hook written into each clone's .git/hooks, instead of core.hooksPath pointing at a repo-carried .githooks directory?

options.label: Git refuses to run hooks from a directory tracked in the repo, so the .githooks dir only worked after a manual copy in each clone

core.hooksPath is per-clone local config and swaps out the clone's entire hooks directory: the opt-in did not travel with the repo and it silenced every other hook. The tracked marker carries the opt-in to every clone, and the hook lands in the clone's own hooks dir, leaving the repo tree and the user's other hooks alone
With hooks tracked in the repo, the remote ran the gate during the push, so checks saw the server's clone instead of the author's

key_points: core.hooksPath is clone-local config, so the opt-in did not travel with the repo: every fresh clone had to opt in again by hand
pointing core.hooksPath at a repo directory replaces the clone's whole hooks dir, silencing whatever other hooks the user had
the tracked marker makes the opt-in travel with the repo to every clone and collaborator, and the hook installs into the clone's own .git/hooks so other hooks keep running and the tree stays clean

questions.prompt: The design treats a clone's .git/hooks as territory it does not own. What rule does write_hook follow there, and what does that boundary protect?

options.label: It backs the existing hook up and installs its own in its place

It rewrites nothing it does not recognize: a foreign pre-push hook stops the install with instructions to merge 'quizgate check || exit 1' in by hand, while its own tagged hook is recognized so reinstalling is a no-op
It appends the gate line to the bottom of any existing hook it finds
It installs a chain that runs the existing hook first and then the gate

key_points: nothing in the clone's hooks dir is ever overwritten or edited: a foreign pre-push hook makes the install fail loudly and tell the author the one line to merge in
its own hook is recognized by its tag comment, so sync can run every session and repeated installs are no-ops (idempotence)
the boundary protects the clone's existing tooling: the user's and other tools' hooks keep working untouched

questions.prompt: An opted-in repo is cloned to a new machine. Pick every statement that holds under the new design.

options.label: With the hook installed but quizgate missing from PATH and from ~/.local/bin, the push is blocked with a pointer to the installer, not let through
Once the marker is committed, the remote blocks pushes of unquizzed commits no matter which clone they come from
Before anything own-your-diff has run in that clone, a push goes through ungated: the marker by itself enforces nothing, only an installed pre-push hook gates
quizgate sync keeps a copy at ~/.local/bin so the pre-push hook can find the gate even outside the session that installed it

key_points: enforcement is per-clone: a clone where install or sync never ran has no gate at all, and the tracked marker only carries the intent
once the hook is in, it fails closed: no reachable quizgate means the push is blocked, never passed through
sync's staged copy is what lets the hook resolve the gate outside an own-your-diff session, so enforcement outlives the session that installed it

questions.prompt: A new requirement arrives: an opted-in repo must keep working on a CI box whose clone already holds the team's own pre-push hook, and no own-your-diff session ever runs there. The teammate runs quizgate install on that box by hand. Walk the design through that box: what does install do to the team's hook, what state is the clone left in, and what would it take for pushes from that box to pass through the gate?
key_points: install refuses to touch the team's hook and fails with the line to merge in, so the clone is left ungated: the seam for coexisting hooks is manual by design, trading that hole for never clobbering foreign tooling
gating that box takes the team merging 'quizgate check || exit 1' into their own hook plus quizgate being reachable there (the copy sync stages, or PATH)
with both in place the gate runs whoever owns the hook file, because enforcement is the quizgate check call, not own-your-diff's hook file
